comparator.name: Dentistry (Tandheelkunde)
comparator.institution: University of Amsterdam through the Academic Centre for Dentistry Amsterdam (ACTA, a UvA-VU collaboration)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026-2027 ACTA OER is the formally adopted source for the compulsory curriculum and confirms that ACTA is a collaboration of the University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. The official study guide confirms a three-year, 180-EC Dutch-taught bachelor. All listed units are compulsory and total 60+60+60=180 EC; there is no open elective space. Year 1 combines cells, tissues, organ systems, oral biology, cariology, microbiology, direct restorations, research methods and statistics, professional development, and two dental-skills lines. Year 2 combines prevention, care planning, immunology and pathology, cariology and periodontology, crowns, periodontitis, the medically complex patient, professional development, preparation for the scientific internship, dental prevention and two further dental-skills lines. Year 3 combines bridges, oral biology and periodontology, medically complex patients, evidence-based dentistry, a 14-EC scientific internship, endodontics, radiology, prevention/treatment and indirect-restoration clinical lines, professional development and professionally assessed conduct. The OER explicitly requires patient care and makes successful preclinical practical work a condition for treating patients.

exception.reason: The defining 180-EC curriculum is entirely compulsory and integrates oral biology, cariology, periodontology, restorative dentistry, endodontology, dental radiology, preventive oral care, clinical care planning, preclinical manual skills and supervised treatment of patients. The current UCR catalogue provides relevant biomedical science, psychology, public health and research methods, but no dentistry, oral biology, dental materials, cariology, periodontology, restorative procedures, endodontology, dental radiology, preclinical simulation or supervised clinical dental care. A 24-course UCR programme could reproduce parts of the biomedical and behavioural context but would omit the profession-defining dental science and clinical skills. It would therefore not be a defensible closest match.
exception.curriculumContext: The formally adopted 2026-2027 ACTA curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: 60 EC in each of three years, with no open elective space. It contains 33 compulsory components spanning biomedical foundations, oral biology and disease, research methods, four progressive dental-skills lines, prevention, care planning, restorative dentistry, periodontology, medically complex patients, evidence-based dentistry, a 14-EC scientific internship, endodontology, radiology, clinical treatment and professionally assessed conduct. Patient care is an explicit curriculum requirement, and access to patient treatment depends on successful preclinical practical work.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current enriched UCR course workbook, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites, planned availability, disciplines, topics and methods. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity, HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics provide relevant biomedical foundations. HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health, HCBPSYC211 Statistics & Experimental Methods, HCBPSYC311 Medical & Health Psychology and HCBPSYC313 Advanced Research Seminar provide public-health, behavioural and research perspectives. None of the 151 courses teaches oral anatomy or biology, cariology, periodontology, dental biomaterials, crowns or bridges, restorative technique, endodontology, dental radiology, dental care planning, preclinical operative skills or supervised treatment of dental patients. The workbook therefore provides no defensible basis for a scheduled 24-course UCR Dentistry programme.
